primaryKeyword: how to know your skin type

analyzedSources.bodySummary: Groups routines by oily, dry, combination, sensitive and normal skin and uses a conventional FAQ structure.
Uses a bare-face method and distinguishes a relatively stable type from changing skin conditions influenced by environment and routine.
Offers a day test and wash test while explicitly noting that skincare-industry labels are not medical terms.
Maps familiar oily, dry, combination, sensitive and normal patterns to product-category choices, but jumps quickly to shopping.
Frames type as a route to routine choices and budget products, illustrating the commercial pressure readers may feel after self-classifying.
Keeps the baseline to cleansing, moisturising and protection, cautions against overwashing, and labels the material general patient information.
Explains why routines vary by oil, hydration and barrier behaviour and recommends a step-by-step routine by skin category.
Uses facial-area observations and blotting paper as a supporting check rather than the only method.
Separates an oily T-zone from normal or dry cheeks and acknowledges sensitive reactions as a cross-cutting concern.
Adds Indian climate and sun context and treats type identification as a preliminary step before a routine.
Uses a 30-minute wait and blotting paper test, then moves to product and routine recommendations.

gaps: Most results treat one at-home test as a definitive label.
Retail pages convert uncertainty straight into product recommendations.
Few pages explain that a changing concern may not be a fixed skin type.
differentiationOpportunities: Present a simple observation exercise as a clue, not a diagnosis.
Separate baseline skin patterns from temporary responses to weather, products, and routine changes.
Give readers permission to start with one simple observation rather than a full product haul.

judgmentChecks.notes: Reviewed eleven organic sources for their test methods, category language, limits, and gaps. The page will use an observation-first, non-diagnostic MyMirror angle.
